title: The Hugging Tree
summary: Alba is new in the neighbourhood and doesn't know anyone. In the most forgotten corner of the park, a very old tree has a branch that knows how to hug.

scenes.text:
In the most forgotten corner of the park there was a very old tree.

It was so old that its trunk was wrinkled, like a grandpa's hands. Its branches were long and grey, and nearly all of them pointed at the sky.

Nearly all of them. But not one.

One branch grew low and curved, close to the ground, like an arm that's waiting.

Many years ago, children used to sit beneath it. But one day they put swings and slides on the other side of the park, and the children went over there.

The tree watched them play from far away. And when the breeze blew, it sighed with all its leaves.

One autumn afternoon, a new girl came to the park. Her name was Alba.

Her family had just moved to the neighbourhood, and Alba didn't know anyone.

She stood watching the swings from far away. The children were playing, shouting, having fun. She didn't dare go closer.

So she went to the most forgotten corner of the park, sat down beneath the old tree and hugged her knees.

Then, very slowly, the low branch moved.

It came down, it curved, and it wrapped itself around Alba's shoulders.

It was a hug.

Alba sat very, very still. Then, very carefully, she hugged the trunk back.

It was rough and warm, like the back of a big dog.

"Hello," she whispered. "I'm Alba. I'm new."

The tree couldn't talk. But it squeezed its branch a tiny bit, and Alba understood what it meant: I was lonely too.

From that day on, Alba went to the tree every afternoon. She told it about school. She showed it her drawings. She read it stories out loud.

And the tree listened, with all its branches still, so as not to miss a single word.

One afternoon, Alba heard crying over by the swings.

It was a little boy with a scraped knee. He had fallen off the slide, and the others carried on playing without noticing.

Alba hesitated. Then she went over.

"Come on," she said. "I want you to meet someone."

She led him by the hand to the forgotten corner. The boy sat down under the tree, still crying.

And the low branch came down, and hugged him.

The boy stopped crying all at once. He looked at the branch. He looked at Alba. And he let out a great big laugh.

"The tree hugged me!"

His name was Teo. He was Alba's first friend in the neighbourhood.

Teo told his sister. His sister told her friends. And her friends told the whole park.

Now, in the corner that used to be forgotten, there's always someone.

The boy who lost at marbles. The girl who misses her grandma. The one who had a bad day and doesn't want to talk about it.

They queue up without pushing, and the low branch hugs them one at a time.

In autumn, that branch is the first to turn orange. You can see it from far away, swaying in the wind.

And Alba isn't the new girl any more. She's the one who knows the tree.
